Import/export works end-to-end: standard-format export with tags and dates, and import that retains title, tags, and the original 2015 saved date, skips duplicates and invalid entries, and sorts correctly by that original date. Here's your walk.

---

### 🔗 http://maker:4001 (refresh)

**Action A — Export your library**
1. Save a couple of tagged links.
2. Click **Export** (top right). A standard **bookmark HTML file** downloads — the same format browsers use, carrying each link's title, address, tags, and saved date.

**Action B — Import a browser bookmark file**
1. Click **Import** and choose a bookmark HTML file exported from a browser (or the one you just exported).
2. The links are added, **keeping their titles, tags, and original saved dates** — an old bookmark shows its real original date, not today's.
3. A status line reports how many were imported and how many were **skipped** (duplicates already in your library, or malformed entries). Sorting by **Oldest first** brings genuinely old imports to the top.

---

### The choices I made — please confirm

- **Round-trip fields are the standard set: title, address, tags, and saved date.** App-specific things — your personal note, reading state, archived state — aren't part of the browser-bookmark format, so a plain export/import doesn't carry those. (A full private backup that preserves everything would be a separate feature; flag it if you want it.)
- **Duplicates are skipped** on import (matched by address), never doubled.
- Tags come from the standard **TAGS** attribute (as Firefox exports). Chrome exports don't include tags or use folders — if you'd want **folder names turned into tags** on import, tell me and I'll add that.

Try an export, then re-import it, and tell me whether this preserves what you need — and whether folder-to-tag mapping matters to you.
